name: seed_drill
source: A coulter seed drill. Its width comes from the model's two work sockets (24 openers at 3 m: tool_spacing_m 0.125), its mass from the vehicle. The hopper, the crop and the rate belong to the game.

range.source: [AS] D497's field speed table was not found; seed drills are usually run at 6-12 km/h (manufacturer ranges), the seeding depth set by the coulters between 2 and 8 cm. Above 12 km/h the seed placement degrades (0.06 of quality per km/h, floor 0.4).

draft.source: [AS] Draft form of ASABE D497, row grain drill. The coefficients are NOT those of the University of Arizona Extension table (the row was not found in the extracts seen): invented so that a 3 m, 24-opener drill pulls about 2-3 kN at 8 km/h and 4 cm, which is the order of conventional coulter drills (about 0.5-1 kN per metre of width). N per opener per cm of depth, primary and secondary tillage. tool_spacing_m is the opener spacing. moisture_factor, compaction_gain, lateral_ratio and creep_speed_m_s are assumptions: the literature found disagrees even on the sign of the moisture effect, so the curve only raises draft above field capacity.

soil.source: [AS] nothing cited: as the cultivator, the weight on the edge and the suction take the coulters down onto the gauge wheels at the set depth; stiff gauge and high damping for stability at 960 Hz.
